# MIT Exokernel literature: local collection

Collected 2026-10-01. Every file was downloaded from pdos.csail.mit.edu: the PDOS papers directory, the exokernel theses archive, or Dawson Engler's old PDOS home page. Most originals are PostScript. These were converted with `ps2pdf`; each Source URL below points to the original. Each `.pdf` has a matching `.txt` made with `pdftotext -layout`.

**About the text files:** several 1994–1999 TeX documents (the theses and the early position papers) use Type 3 bitmap fonts, so their fi/fl/ff ligatures are lost in extraction ("ecient", "exible", "rst"). A word-boundary fix-up pass restored about 1,200 common words (efficient, flexible, first, define, specific, ...) in 12 files. Rarer ligature words in those files may still be broken. Venues below come from each paper's own header or from Engler's PDOS home page. Where a document does not state its venue, the entry says so.

`pdos-exokernel-project-pages.txt` is a text snapshot of https://pdos.csail.mit.edu/archive/exo/ , /archive/exo/docs.html , /archive/exo/theses/index.html and https://pdos.csail.mit.edu/~engler/ , with links shown inline. Use it as an index of the original project pages.

## Core exokernel papers and Engler's theses

| File | Citation | Source URL | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|
| `engler-1994-osdi-exokernel-approach-extensibility.pdf` | D. R. Engler, M. F. Kaashoek, J. W. O'Toole Jr. "The Exokernel Approach to Operating System Extensibility." 1-page panel statement/precis, Proc. 1st Symposium on Operating Systems Design and Implementation (OSDI), Nov. 1994 (venue per Engler's home page; dblp lists it at p. 198). | https://pdos.csail.mit.edu/~engler/osdi-exo.ps | A one-page statement of the exokernel idea. Kernels should embed minimal functionality and push the OS interface down so that only hardware-defined resources are exported. Resources (pages, time slices, TLB, context IDs, disk blocks) are protected by 64-bit capabilities, and the only non-physical kernel functions are exception forwarding and upcalls. |
| `engler-1994-aegis-secure-programmable-exokernel-draft.pdf` | D. R. Engler, M. F. Kaashoek, J. W. O'Toole Jr. "Aegis: A Secure Programmable Exokernel." Manuscript dated June 27, 1994. The document names no venue. The OSDI'94 precis cites an EW'94 paper of this title; this file may be a draft of it. | https://pdos.csail.mit.edu/papers/exo.ps | The earliest exokernel write-up in the collection. Applications manage hardware directly rather than through layers of OS software, and they customize the OS by extending exokernel interfaces. Code inspection, inlined cross-domain procedure calls and safe languages make it safe to run user code in the kernel. It introduces the Aegis prototype. |
| `engler-1994-osr-kernel-as-secure-programmable-machine.pdf` | D. R. Engler, M. F. Kaashoek, J. W. O'Toole Jr. "The Operating System Kernel as a Secure Programmable Machine." ACM SIGOPS Operating Systems Review, special issue on extensible operating systems. Engler's page describes it as a later version of a position paper in the Proc. 6th SIGOPS European Workshop, 1994. The year in the filename refers to that workshop, and the OSR issue date is not stated in the file. | https://pdos.csail.mit.edu/papers/osr-exo.ps (identical to /papers/xsigops.ps) | A position paper arguing that most OS performance and flexibility problems go away when the OS interface is pushed lower, so that user-level libraries and servers build abstractions over the exposed hardware. Applications may download additions to the supervisor-mode environment, kept safe by code inspection, inlined cross-domain calls and safe languages. Engler himself notes that its philosophy is somewhat out of date. |
| `engler-1995-ms-thesis-prototype-exokernel.pdf` | Dawson R. Engler. "The Design and Implementation of a Prototype Exokernel Operating System." S.M. thesis, MIT EECS, January 1995. | https://pdos.csail.mit.edu/~engler/msthesis.ps (a scanned copy is also at https://dspace.mit.edu/bitstream/handle/1721.1/41351/34889746-MIT.pdf) | Proposes the exokernel structure: the OS should only multiplex the raw hardware, not abstract it, and library OSes implement abstractions. It motivates the design, gives design precepts, and covers general multiplexing issues. It then describes and measures the Aegis/ExOS prototype on DECstations. Engler calls it a longer version of the SOSP'95 paper that is about 6 months behind it. |
| `engler-1995-hotos-exterminate-all-os-abstractions.pdf` | D. R. Engler, M. F. Kaashoek. "Exterminate All Operating System Abstractions." Proc. 5th Workshop on Hot Topics in Operating Systems (HotOS-V), 1995. | https://pdos.csail.mit.edu/papers/hotos-jeremiad.ps | The polemical philosophy paper. It argues that defining an OS as software that both multiplexes and abstracts resources is the "defining tragedy" behind decades of poor performance, reliability and adaptability. Its proposed fix is to remove OS abstractions entirely by lowering the interface to the hardware level. |
| `engler-1995-hotos-avm-application-level-virtual-memory.pdf` | D. R. Engler, S. K. Gupta, M. F. Kaashoek. "AVM: Application-Level Virtual Memory." Proc. HotOS-V, 1995. | https://pdos.csail.mit.edu/papers/hotos-uvm.ps (same paper as ~engler/avm.ps) | Argues that microkernel page servers are still rigid or privileged, while minimal VM systems lack features such as copy-on-write. It proposes moving the whole VM system out of the kernel into application libraries, including page-table structure. Applications can then pick or write VM policies, and the kernel gets simpler. |
| `engler-1995-sosp-exokernel-architecture.pdf` | D. R. Engler, M. F. Kaashoek, J. O'Toole Jr. "Exokernel: An Operating System Architecture for Application-Level Resource Management." Proc. 15th ACM Symposium on Operating Systems Principles (SOSP), December 1995. | https://pdos.csail.mit.edu/papers/exokernel-sosp95.ps (Engler's copy at ~engler/sosp-95.ps differs slightly in layout) | The defining exokernel paper. A small kernel securely exports hardware to untrusted library OSes through a low-level interface (secure bindings, visible resource revocation, abort protocol), separating protection from management. Measurements on Aegis/ExOS show primitive operations 10–100x faster than Ultrix, and VM and IPC can be implemented efficiently at application level. |
| `kaashoek-1997-sosp-application-performance-flexibility-exokernel.pdf` | M. F. Kaashoek, D. R. Engler, G. R. Ganger, H. M. Briceño, R. Hunt, D. Mazières, T. Pinckney, R. Grimm, J. Jannotti, K. Mackenzie. "Application Performance and Flexibility on Exokernel Systems." Proc. 16th ACM SOSP, October 1997. | https://pdos.csail.mit.edu/papers/exo-sosp97/exo-sosp97.ps (an HTML version is in the same directory, and ~engler/sosp-97.ps is another rendering) | Introduces Xok (x86 exokernel) and ExOS, and compares end-to-end application performance with FreeBSD and OpenBSD. Unmodified UNIX programs run comparably or better, and specialized ones run much faster (for example, a factor of eight for the Cheetah web server). It also presents XN, which multiplexes the disk safely using untrusted deterministic functions (UDFs) for library-defined metadata, and gives lessons from building three exokernel systems. |
| `engler-1998-phd-thesis-exokernel-architecture.pdf` | Dawson R. Engler. "The Exokernel Operating System Architecture." Ph.D. thesis, MIT EECS, October 1998. | https://pdos.csail.mit.edu/archive/exo/theses/engler/thesis.ps | The full statement of the architecture: resource management becomes unprivileged but safe because the exokernel protects resources and untrusted software manages them. It covers how to build an exokernel, whether a real one can be built, and whether it is worthwhile, drawing on Aegis and Xok. Results include a web server an order of magnitude faster, unmodified Unix applications up to 3x faster, and global performance up to 5x better. It also details protection techniques such as untrusted deterministic functions. |
| `engler-1995-sosp-talk-slides-exokernels.pdf` | D. Engler, F. Kaashoek, J. O'Toole. "Exokernels" (SOSP'95 talk slides). | https://pdos.csail.mit.edu/~engler/exo-sosp-talk.ps | Slides for the SOSP'95 talk. They summarize the argument that OS abstractions preempt application design, then cover secure multiplexing without abstraction, library OSes, and the Aegis/ExOS structure and results. |
| `engler-1997-sosp-talk-slides-why-exokernels-matter.pdf` | D. Engler et al. "Why Exokernels Matter" (SOSP'97 talk slides). | https://pdos.csail.mit.edu/~engler/sosp97-talk.ps | Slides for the SOSP'97 talk. They ask whether exokernels give applications real control and whether that matters, then cover separating protection from management, disk multiplexing (XN), Xok/ExOS, and application performance. |

## Networking: DPF, ASH, server OS, application-level networking

| File | Citation | Source URL | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|
| `engler-1996-sigcomm-dpf-dynamic-packet-filters.pdf` | D. R. Engler, M. F. Kaashoek. "DPF: Fast, Flexible Message Demultiplexing using Dynamic Code Generation." Proc. ACM SIGCOMM '96, August 1996. | https://pdos.csail.mit.edu/papers/dpf.ps (Engler's copy ~engler/dpf-sigcomm96.ps is a near-identical rendering) | Packet filters let new protocols be implemented outside the kernel, but interpreting them is too slow for high-performance systems. DPF uses dynamic code generation to compile filters into native demultiplexing code, matching or beating hand-coded demultiplexers. DPF is the exokernel's mechanism for securely multiplexing the network. |
| `wallach-1996-sigcomm-ash-application-specific-handlers.pdf` | D. A. Wallach, D. R. Engler, M. F. Kaashoek. "ASHs: Application-Specific Handlers for High-Performance Messaging." Proc. ACM SIGCOMM '96, August 1996. | https://pdos.csail.mit.edu/papers/ash-sigcomm96.ps | ASHs are user-written message handlers. They are downloaded into the kernel and run right after demultiplexing, with their operations controlled and their runtime bounded to keep them safe. They can direct message transfers (avoiding copies), send replies (cutting send-response latency) and integrate data-manipulation steps dynamically. The Aegis prototype beats high-performance UDP/TCP libraries that do not use ASHs. |
| `engler-1996-dynamic-protocol-composition-manuscript.pdf` | D. R. Engler, D. A. Wallach, M. F. Kaashoek. "Design and Implementation of a Modular, Flexible, and Fast System for Dynamic Protocol Composition." Unpublished manuscript. The document names no venue, and it cites 1996 work. Engler's page says it explores parts of the ASH implementation in more depth. | https://pdos.csail.mit.edu/~engler/ash-osdi.ps | Describes how the ASH system composes protocols dynamically and modularly. Each protocol's data-processing steps (checksum, byte-swap, encryption, ...) are fused at run time into one specialized loop that touches each byte at most once. It reports performance comparable to hand-coded protocol stacks, and says the system is integrated into Aegis on Ethernet and AN2. |
| `kaashoek-1996-sigops-ew-server-operating-systems.pdf` | M. F. Kaashoek, D. R. Engler, G. R. Ganger, D. A. Wallach. "Server Operating Systems." Proc. 1996 ACM SIGOPS European Workshop, Sept. 9–11, 1996 (venue per Engler's page). | https://pdos.csail.mit.edu/papers/serverOS-sigops96.ps | Introduces "server operating systems": abstractions and runtime support for specialized high-performance servers, built on the exokernel. Features include aggressive specialization, direct device-to-device access, an event-driven structure and compiler-assisted ILP. An HTTP server built this way outperforms conventional-OS servers by more than an order of magnitude. |
| `ganger-2002-tocs-fast-flexible-application-level-networking.pdf` | G. R. Ganger, D. R. Engler, M. F. Kaashoek, H. M. Briceño, R. Hunt, T. Pinckney. "Fast and Flexible Application-Level Networking on Exokernel Systems." ACM Transactions on Computer Systems 20(1):49–83, February 2002. | https://pdos.csail.mit.edu/papers/exo:tocs.pdf | A retrospective on Xok/ExOS application-level networking: the kernel mechanisms and library-OS organization, with lessons learned, both positive and negative. It covers three specialized services: the Cheetah HTTP server, the webswamp benchmarking tool and an application-level TCP forwarder. Each reaches the platform's maximum end-to-end performance, and Cheetah has 2–4x the throughput of conventional servers. |
| `wallach-1997-phd-thesis-application-specific-networking.pdf` | Deborah A. Wallach. "High-Performance Application-Specific Networking." Ph.D. thesis, MIT EECS, January 1997. | https://pdos.csail.mit.edu/archive/exo/theses/kerr/thesis.ps | The full treatment of ASHs. Application protocols are downloaded safely into the kernel and tightly integrated with the communication system, which removes kernel crossings and scheduling delays and lets copying be merged with other data manipulation. It describes the ASH implementation in Aegis and an alternative, fast asynchronous upcalls. |

## Storage and related

| File | Citation | Source URL | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|
| `grimm-1996-meng-thesis-exodisk.pdf` | Robert Grimm. "Exodisk: Maximizing Application Control over Storage Management." S.B./M.Eng. thesis, MIT EECS, May 1996. | https://pdos.csail.mit.edu/archive/exo/theses/rgrimm/thesis.ps | A disk system that separates protection from management. It space-multiplexes raw storage as self-protected extents, plus a lightweight i-node layer that lets applications combine extents and co-locate their own metadata. Protection costs under 10%, and the thesis demonstrates fast file insertion, disk-directed I/O and application-specific persistence. |
| `ganger-1997-usenix-cffs-embedded-inodes-explicit-grouping.pdf` | G. R. Ganger, M. F. Kaashoek. "Embedded Inodes and Explicit Grouping: Exploiting Disk Bandwidth for Small Files." Proc. USENIX Technical Conference, January 1997, pp. 1–17. | https://pdos.csail.mit.edu/papers/cffs-usenix97.ps | Related work from the same group rather than an exokernel paper. It presents C-FFS, the file system used in the Xok/ExOS work. Embedded inodes put inodes in directories, and explicit grouping places small files from one directory adjacently, raising small-file throughput by 5–7x. |

| File | Citation | Source URL | Summary |

| `briceno-1997-meng-thesis-decentralizing-unix-abstractions.pdf` | Héctor Manuel Briceño Pulido. "Decentralizing UNIX Abstractions in the Exokernel Architecture." S.B./M.Eng. thesis, MIT EECS, February 1997. | https://pdos.csail.mit.edu/archive/exo/theses/hbriceno/thesis.ps | Studies how to move UNIX abstractions out of the kernel into library code while keeping correct semantics, despite state being shared among mutually distrustful processes. It describes ExOS 1.0, a prototype library OS complete enough to run editors and compilers. |
| `pinckney-1997-meng-thesis-extensibility-event-capture.pdf` | Thomas Pinckney III. "Operating System Extensibility Through Event Capture." S.B./M.Eng. thesis, MIT EECS, February 1997. (The theses index swaps the titles of Pinckney's two files: this file is thesis.ps.) | https://pdos.csail.mit.edu/archive/exo/theses/pinckney/thesis.ps | Offers guidelines for designing extensibility into an OS: find the likely extension targets, expose them as attach points, and structure the system so extensions run efficiently and safely. As a demonstration it builds an extension for application-level process scheduling. |
| `pinckney-1997-thesis-proposal-hierarchical-untrusted-resource-mgmt.pdf` | Thomas Pinckney. "Hierarchical Untrusted Resource Management." Thesis proposal, January 15, 1997. (File proposal.ps; the index labels it "MS thesis" with the other title.) | https://pdos.csail.mit.edu/archive/exo/theses/pinckney/proposal.ps | Proposes letting applications set resource-management policy for groups of applications, for example a `make` managing its children's memory. It also aims to make OS extension practical for ordinary programmers. |
| `wyatt-1997-meng-thesis-shared-libraries-exokernel.pdf` | Douglas Karl Wyatt. "Shared Libraries in an Exokernel Operating System." M.Eng. thesis, MIT EECS, September 1997 (submitted Aug. 28, 1997). | https://pdos.csail.mit.edu/archive/exo/theses/dwyatt/thesis.ps | Statically linking a large LibOS into every program wastes memory and disk. Making the LibOS a shared library has a bootstrapping problem, because loading needs the file and VM systems the LibOS provides. The thesis solves it with a Shared Library Server that supplies basic file I/O and VM for loading. |
| `jannotti-1998-meng-thesis-exokernel-principles-conventional-os.pdf` | John Jannotti. "Applying Exokernel Principles to Conventional Operating Systems." M.Eng. thesis, MIT EECS, February 1998. | https://pdos.csail.mit.edu/archive/exo/theses/jj/thesis.ps (a PDF at /papers/jj-meng-exo-feb98.pdf has broken font encoding, so the PS was used) | Brings exokernel ideas into Linux step by step instead of redesigning it. XN (raw disk) and DPF (raw network) are integrated with Unix abstractions. DPF integration is cheap and lets Cheetah specialize its TCP/IP stack for worthwhile gains. |
| `candea-1998-meng-thesis-sharing-protected-abstractions-pam.pdf` | George M. Candea. "Flexible and Efficient Sharing of Protected Abstractions." S.B./M.Eng. thesis, MIT EECS, May 1998. | https://pdos.csail.mit.edu/archive/exo/theses/candea/thesis.ps (the same thesis is at /papers/ProtAbs.pdf, whose fonts do not extract) | Decentralized control makes it hard for mutually distrustful applications to share abstractions. The thesis presents PAM (protected abstraction mechanism), which lets unprivileged applications define and securely share generic abstractions at run time. It avoids context switches and optimizes for repeated invocation. (This thesis is about PAM, not XN; XN is described in the SOSP'97 paper and in Engler's PhD thesis.) |
| `coffing-1999-meng-thesis-x86-vmm-exokernel.pdf` | Charles L. Coffing. "An x86 Protected Mode Virtual Machine Monitor for the MIT Exokernel." S.B./M.Eng. thesis, MIT EECS, May 1999. | https://pdos.csail.mit.edu/papers/exo:coffing-meng.ps | An x86 VMM that runs several OSes concurrently on Xok, with Linux as the reference guest. Xok was modified to allow controlled sharing of the GDT, LDT and IDT. The monitor is untrusted and shares a page table with Xok and the guest to reduce TLB flushes. |
| `chen-2000-meng-thesis-multiprocessing-exokernel.pdf` | Benjie Chen. "Multiprocessing with the Exokernel Operating System." S.B./M.Eng. thesis, MIT EECS, February 2000 (signed May 1999). | https://pdos.csail.mit.edu/papers/exo:chen-meng.pdf | A symmetric-multiprocessor Xok, showing that unprivileged library OSes remain viable on SMP. It covers in-kernel synchronization and new interfaces for message passing, kernel thread support and multiprocessor scheduling. It also gives a synchronization strategy for mutually untrusting processes, where voluntary locks break down. |
